statements.status_notes: CVE-2024-26458 is a memory leak in xdr_rmtcallres() in libgssrpc (src/lib/rpc/pmap_rmt.c): the decoded port pointer is stored only after the following field also decodes, so it leaks if that decode fails. MIT fixed it in commit https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/c5f9c816107f70139de11b38aa02db2f1774ee0d, first released in krb5 1.22, whose message describes the function as unused within the krb5 tree. Debian marks trixie's 1.21.3-5+deb13u1 vulnerable, with urgency unimportant (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2024-26458). This owner is built from that Debian version; the MIT 1.21.3 source of xdr_rmtcallres() lacks the change, and neither Debian's patches nor this owner's backports touch that file, so every matched build carries the leak. Pending: a decision whether to backport the upstream change or to record MIT's reasoning; xdr_rmtcallres() is exported by the libgssrpc4t64 library (as gssrpc_xdr_rmtcallres), so code outside the krb5 tree can call it, and a not-affected statement needs a recorded maintainer decision.
